full_judgment: Facts in short are that plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land, alleging inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to one Soku Mondal under landlord Nasiruddin Mondal. After Soku Mondal's death the landlord possessed it in khas when the superior interest was auction purchased by one Bibhuti Bhushan and he settled the same with the plaintiff in the year 1357 B.S. at rental of Tk. 5/- and since 1357 B.S. plaintiff had been possessing the suit land on payment of rent though the land was erroneously recorded in the names of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who are the sons of the Bibhuti Bhushan when the custodian of enemy property declared the land as an enemy property. Hence the suit the suit was contested by defendant No. 3 who alleged that the land was correctly recorded in the name of the sons of Bibhuti Bhushan who are now Indian nationals since 1965 and hence the government considered the suit land as enemy property. The court of first instance dismissed the suit and the same was affirmed by the learned District Judge against which Kalimuddin Sarder has moved this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and had obtained this Rule.
